question.text: If the freezing point of a <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>01</mn></math> molal aqueous solution of a cobalt (III) bromide-ammonia complex (which behaves as a strong electrolyte) is  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>-</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0557</mn><mo>°</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> , the number of bromide(s) in the coordination sphere of the complex is [ <math><msub><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">f</mi></mrow></msub></math> for water <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>.86</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">K</mi></math>  <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>kg</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">l</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> ]

solution.text:
ΔTf=iKfm
0.0557=i×1.86×0.01
i=3, means complex will give 3-ions 

Hence, formula should be CoNH35BrBr2
